designs.name: Nakagin Capsule Tower
designs.description: 🏺 The digital shadow of the former Nakagin Capsule Tower which was a mixed-use residential and office tower designed by architect Kisho Kurokawa and located in Shimbashi, Tokyo, Japan. Completed in 1972, the building was a rare remaining example of Japanese Metabolism, an architectural movement emblematic of Japan's postwar cultural resurgence.

designs.name: Slanted
designs.description: 🚕 A sloped variant of the Nakagin Capsule Tower where the capsules have balconies and the towers are graduated in opposing directions. Each tower has a direction and every floor is stepped in this direction.

designs.name: Twisted
designs.description: 🚙 A twisted variant of the Nakagin Capsule Tower where the capsules are trapezoids and towers are round with the floors twisting in one direction.

designs.name: Dancing
designs.description: 🚓 The expolsion axonometry of a futuristic variant of the Nakagin Capsule Tower where two towers are dancing with each other. The capsules are ellipsoids around a round shaft and a blob base.

designs.name: Capsule Dream
designs.description: 🚗 A wild dream of capsule towers.
